script: Your dog passed out upside down, legs in the air, looking completely ridiculous, and that position actually tells you a lot. Sleeping belly-up with paws flopped open is one of the most vulnerable positions an animal can be in, so a dog only does it when they feel completely safe, it's basically the ultimate trust pose. It also helps them cool down faster, exposing the belly and paw pads, the areas with the least fur, releases heat quickly. Dogs that curl into a tight ball instead are doing the opposite, conserving body heat and instinctively protecting their vital organs, an old habit left over from sleeping exposed in the wild. So next time you catch your dog sprawled out like they lost a fight with gravity, that's not weird, that's your dog telling you this is the safest place in the world.
